market_sentiment.regime_cn: 极度恐慌（防御避险为主）
summary_notes_cn: 期权波动层面：标普500恐慌指数收于 26.80（单日 -5.27%），纳指100波动率指数收于 38.53，科技股相对大盘仍保有 +11.73 点的额外波动溢价。
尾部风险层面：黑天鹅偏度指数报 142.06，显示机构防范极端尾部暴跌的对冲需求偏高。
利率与美债层面：10年期美债收益率报 4.85%，10年期减13周美债期限利差为 +69 个基点，收益率曲线维持正斜率（未倒挂）。
跨资产信用层面：高收益公司债与长期国债比值报 0.9304（单日 -0.80%），长端国债表现强于高收益债，债市资金偏向防御避险。

federal_register_trade_tech.source_cn: 美国联邦公报（商务部与贸易代表办公室法定文件）
federal_register_trade_tech.title_raw: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
federal_register_trade_tech.abstract_raw: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. Third, this IFR amends the presumptions which front-end chips fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips. These amendments reduce the number of pathways to overcome the presumptions for chip designers located in destinations which face a license requirement for SI chips. This change gives the U.S. government critical oversight over companies headquartered in certain countries that seek to leverage advanced semiconductor production capabilities in third countries. Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced. The regulatory changes in this rule formalize the rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, which the Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced in May 2025.

federal_register_trade_tech.source_cn: 美国联邦公报（商务部与贸易代表办公室法定文件）
federal_register_trade_tech.title_raw: Applications for Inclusion on the Binational Panels Roster Under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement
federal_register_trade_tech.abstract_raw: The United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) provides for the establishment of a roster of individuals to serve on binational panels convened to review final determinations in antidumping or countervailing duty (AD/CVD) proceedings and amendments to AD/CVD statutes of a USMCA Party. The United States annually renews its selections for the roster. USTR invites applications from eligible individuals wishing to be included on the roster for the period April 1, 2027, through March 31, 2028.

federal_register_trade_tech.title_raw: Notice of Product Exclusion Extensions: China's Acts, Policies, and Practices Related to Technology Transfer, Intellectual Property, and Innovation
federal_register_trade_tech.abstract_raw: In prior notices, the U.S. Trade Representative (Trade Representative) modified the actions in the Section 301 investigation of China's acts, policies, and practices related to technology transfer, intellectual property, and innovation by excluding from additional duties certain products of China. While most exclusions have expired in prior years, certain exclusions remain in force. This notice announces the Trade Representative's determination to further extend all 178 current exclusions.
